text: Tom Gribilas was a pillar of the Scarborough soccer community. In 1983, he co-founded the Olympic Flame Soccer Club and was its president, and the club’s heart and soul, for the past 33 years. Under Tom’s guidance, the Club won many league titles and tournaments, including provincial and Canadian championships. Tom was also involved in the creation of the Central Soccer League and a long-time Director of the Scarborough Soccer Association. For 40 years, Tom tirelessly, and with little fanfare, volunteered countless time to the youth of Scarborough and East York and the sport of soccer. For his exceptional contributions, he was awarded the City of Scarborough Parks and Culture Award in 1993, a Government of Canada Volunteer Award and the City of Toronto Award of Merit in 2001, and the Ontario Soccer Association Centre Circle Award for Meritorious Service in 2013. City Council direct the General Manager, Parks, Forestry and Recreation to investigate the feasibility of assigning the name “Tom Gribilas Field” to the unnamed soccer pitch at Ellesmere Community Centre and to report with recommendation to the Scarborough Community Council at its March 19, 2019 meeting.
